clue.text: Quick-witted librarian conclusively punches crook violating novel

parts.note: a quick-witted person is bright, clever

indicators.note: one piece punches into another, so it sits inside it
violating suggests the word crook is abused and knocked out of shape
conclusively points to the closing letter of the word librarian

explanation.surface: A sharp librarian finally lands a blow on a crook who is breaking the law.
explanation.walkthrough: 'violating' rearranges the word crook (to OROCK), and 'punches' puts the last letter of librarian inside that. BRIGHTON ROCK is Graham Greene's 1938 novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Graham Greene's well-known crime story set in a seaside town is titled this, so it is an example of a novel.

clue.text: Architectural style a university head regularly sees in coach

indicators.note: the coach sees these letters in, admitting them so that they sit inside it

parts.note: a coach is a long-distance bus

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of the word head, starting from the first

explanation.surface: A university chief often spots an architectural style while riding in a coach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coach' suggests a trainer, but it is a bus. 'regularly' picks the first and third letters of head.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bauhaus was the German design school whose name labels a modernist building style.

clue.text: Clearly defined data you texted is received by surveyor

parts.note: info, short for information, means data

indicators.note: is received by puts the text-speak letter inside the surveyor's abbreviation

parts.note: CS stands for Chartered Surveyor
in text-message shorthand you is written as the letter U

explanation.surface: Information you sent by text message reaches the surveyor, sharp and unambiguous.
explanation.definitionFit: A photograph or idea that is sharp and distinct is said to be in focus.

clue.text: Robert/Bill overcome by split personality here in India

indicators.note: in a down clue, being overcome by means sitting underneath, so these pieces come after the first

parts.note: Mr Hyde is the evil half of Dr Jekyll's divided self in Stevenson's tale
Rab is a Scottish pet form of Robert
AD, short for advertisement, is a bill or poster

explanation.surface: Someone called Robert or Bill is defeated by a person with a split personality somewhere in India.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry, 'overcome by' puts RAB and AD under HYDE. RAB is a Scottish short form of Robert.
explanation.definitionFit: Hyderabad is a large city in southern India, the place the clue points to.

clue.text: Metal on banger? Some players are given this

parts.note: Os is the chemical symbol of osmium, a metal
a banger is British slang for an old, battered car

explanation.surface: Someone asks about metal sitting on an old car, then notes that some performers get one.
explanation.walkthrough: A banger is British slang for a clapped-out old car (as well as a sausage). The players are actors.
explanation.definitionFit: Film actors receive the Academy Award statuette, known by this nickname, for their performances.

clue.text: Moving article describes musical performance

indicators.note: moving suggests the letters of article are shifted around into a new order

explanation.surface: A touching newspaper piece describes a concert.
explanation.definitionFit: A recital is a solo or small-group concert, a kind of musical performance.

clue.text: Sculptor in ice, fashionable around fifties

indicators.note: around signals that the reshaped letters wrap round the Roman numerals
to fashion something is to shape it, so the words in ice are reshaped

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty, so two fifties are LL

explanation.surface: An artist works in ice, a trendy medium, sometime around the 1950s.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fashionable' looks like IN but reshapes 'in ice' to CEINI, and 'around' wraps that round LL. Benvenuto Cellini was a Renaissance goldsmith and sculptor.
explanation.definitionFit: Benvenuto Cellini was an Italian Renaissance goldsmith famous for his bronze Perseus statue.

clue.text: Forgetful person — in bar, potentially

indicators.note: potentially admits that scattering the letters of brain could, among other outcomes, give the words in bar

parts.note: read as an instruction, the answer tells you to scatter the letters of brain, which could give the words in bar

explanation.surface: Someone absent-minded is likely to be found in a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a reverse clue: the answer works as a clue whose solution is the clue's words. Scattering the letters of BRAIN might give IN BAR, as 'potentially' hints.
explanation.definitionFit: A scatterbrain is a disorganised, absent-minded person who keeps forgetting things.

clue.text: Very glad the sulks during last month passed over

indicators.note: during puts the sulking piece inside the flipped month
passed over suggests the month's abbreviation is flipped right over, reading backwards

parts.note: December, abbreviated DEC, is the last month of the year
being in a huff is having a fit of sulks

explanation.surface: Someone is delighted that the bad mood of December has gone by.
explanation.walkthrough: 'passed over' gives CED, the month flipped. CHUFFED is British slang for pleased.
explanation.definitionFit: Chuffed is British informal slang for very pleased or delighted.

clue.text: Officer outside to check the French seafood

parts.note: CO stands for Commanding Officer

indicators.note: outside takes just the outer letters of the word check

parts.note: les is the French plural definite article, the

explanation.surface: An officer steps outdoors to inspect the French shellfish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' gives CK, the first and last letters of 'check'; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Cockles are small edible bivalve shellfish, a kind of seafood sold at British seasides.

clue.text: Daredevil outside in shower keeps clean section of footwear?

indicators.note: keeps means those outer letters hold the other pieces within them
outside in takes only the outer letters of the word shower

parts.note: to wash is to clean
a buckle is the fastening part of a shoe

explanation.surface: A thrill-seeker in the shower keeps cleaning a bit of his shoe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside in' gives S and R, the ends of 'shower', and 'keeps' sets the other pieces between them; the question mark flags a buckle as only loosely footwear.
explanation.definitionFit: A swashbuckler is a bold, swaggering adventurer, a daring hero of pirate films.

clue.text: Animal caught short in marine vehicle

indicators.note: in places the animal and the caught letter inside the sailor

parts.note: tar is a slang name for a sailor, someone of the sea
a ram is a male sheep, an animal
C is the short form of caught on a cricket scorecard

explanation.surface: A creature caught out short of a toilet in a marine vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'caught short' is a British idiom for urgently needing a toilet; here it means the abbreviation C. 'in' puts RAM and C inside TAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A tramcar is a single carriage of a tram, a passenger vehicle running on rails.

clue.text: Regrets, in afternoon, imbibing wine

indicators.note: imbibing means drinking in, so the phrase holds the answer within its letters

explanation.surface: Someone has regrets after drinking wine in the afternoon.
explanation.definitionFit: Retsina is a Greek white wine flavoured with pine resin.

clue.text: Contracts less Liberal moderates

indicators.note: less means the Liberal letter is taken away

parts.note: leases are rental contracts

explanation.surface: Political agreements without the Liberals are run by moderates.
explanation.definitionFit: To moderate pain or tension is to lessen or relieve it, a synonym here as a verb.

clue.text: Man's unprofessional, reporting Winter Olympic event

indicators.note: reporting signals that the words are spoken out loud

parts.note: Bob is a man's name, here with a possessive; lay means amateur, not professional, as in a lay person

explanation.surface: A journalist reports that a man is not professional, covering the Winter Olympics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reporting' signals a sound-alike: 'Bob's lay' said out loud.
explanation.definitionFit: Bobsleigh is a team sled race down an icy track, contested at every Winter Olympics.

clue.text: BBC allowed close to patrol Asian bovine, a devilish beast

indicators.note: allowed means the broadcaster's nickname lets the other pieces in

parts.note: the Beeb is the nickname of the BBC

indicators.note: close to takes the last letter of the word patrol

parts.note: a zebu is a humped ox of Asia

explanation.surface: The BBC let a patrol get close to an Asian ox, a fiendish animal.
explanation.walkthrough: The Beeb is a British nickname for the BBC. 'close to' gives L, the end of patrol.
explanation.definitionFit: Beelzebub is a name for the Devil, prince of demons, hence a devilish creature.

clue.text: Chap twitching long after seeing account overdrawn

indicators.note: after seeing puts the longing piece after the account and overdrawn pieces

parts.note: a bill is an account of money owed
OD is a bank-statement abbreviation for overdrawn
to long for something is to be dying for it, so long gives die

explanation.surface: A man feels anxious for a long while after spotting his bank account in the red.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Twitching' is birdwatching, not nervousness: Bill Oddie is a well-known British birdwatcher and TV presenter.
explanation.definitionFit: Bill Oddie, comedian and TV naturalist, is Britain's best-known twitcher, a keen birdwatcher.

clue.text: In company of ally composing, wordsmith Tim's endlessly this

indicators.note: composing suggests putting the letters together in a fresh arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: endlessly drops the final letter of the lyricist's surname

parts.note: Tim Rice is the lyricist who wrote with Andrew Lloyd Webber

explanation.surface: Teamed with a friend, the lyricist Tim Rice is forever poetic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts RICE to RIC, and 'composing' mixes RIC with ALLY. The definition 'this' points back at the clue: what Tim Rice is.
explanation.definitionFit: A lyricist writes song words, so being lyrical, poetic and song-like, fits his trade.

clue.text: Press stifles miscreant, then becoming successful

indicators.note: stifles means the publisher's letters smother the mixed piece inside them

parts.note: OUP is Oxford University Press

indicators.note: a miscreant behaves badly, so the word then is treated roughly and jumbled

explanation.surface: The newspapers hush up a villain, who then prospers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Press' looks like a verb but is a publisher; 'miscreant' is an unusual anagram signal meaning badly behaved.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone on the up is improving their fortunes, rising and doing well.

clue.text: Bloomer enthusiast, between you and me, experienced setback

indicators.note: experienced setback signals the whole assembly suffers a reverse, read back to front
between puts the enthusiast inside the pronoun's letters

parts.note: us means you and me together
a fan is an enthusiast

explanation.surface: Confidentially, a keen fan suffered a reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'experienced setback' turns UFANS round. 'Bloomer' looks like a loaf or old-fashioned knickers but is a blunder.
explanation.definitionFit: A bloomer is a silly blunder, and snafu is slang for a muddle or foul-up.

clue.text: Fruit to add into peanut-based dish mostly

indicators.note: into puts the adding word inside the shortened dish
mostly drops the last letter of the dish's name

parts.note: satay is skewered meat with peanut sauce
to sum is to add up

explanation.surface: Fruit to be added to a peanut dish, for the most part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims the dish to SATA by dropping its final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A satsuma is a small loose-skinned citrus fruit, a kind of mandarin.

clue.text: Type of science one finds in computer department

indicators.note: the one finds a place in the computer's name, sitting within it

parts.note: Apple is a computer brand, as in the Mac
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone finds a branch of science in the IT department.
explanation.definitionFit: Applied science puts research into practical use, as opposed to pure science.

clue.text: Reggae latterly classified as pop?

indicators.note: latterly takes the final letters of the word reggae, here its last two

parts.note: rated means classified or graded

explanation.surface: Late on, reggae music was categorised as pop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pop' is not music but fizzy drink: aerated means made bubbly. 'latterly' takes AE from the end of 'Reggae'.
explanation.definitionFit: Fizzy soft drinks are charged with gas, so they are carbonated like pop.

clue.text: Sad song, for example, to deliver standing up

indicators.note: in a down clue, standing up means the pieces read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: to rid is to free or deliver

explanation.surface: A mournful song, for instance, to perform on one's feet.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry, 'standing up' reads the pieces from the bottom, so they appear backwards in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: A dirge is a slow mournful song, a lament for the dead.

clue.text: Olympic runner trained to peak beyond the 26th?

indicators.note: beyond puts the mixed letters after the twenty-sixth letter

parts.note: Z is the twenty-sixth letter of the alphabet

indicators.note: trained suggests the letters to peak are coached into a new shape

explanation.surface: An athlete is coached to hit peak form after the 26th of the month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trained' rearranges TO PEAK to ATOPEK, and 'beyond' sets it after Z. Emil Zátopek won three golds at the 1952 Olympics.
explanation.definitionFit: Emil Zatopek, Czech distance runner, won 5,000m, 10,000m and marathon golds in 1952.

clue.text: Such a bomb perhaps blocked, with UN backing

indicators.note: with UN backing means those two letters are turned back to front

parts.note: a blocked pipe is not clear, unclear

explanation.surface: A bomb may have been stopped with United Nations support.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with UN backing' reverses the UN at the front of UNCLEAR, making NU.
explanation.definitionFit: An atomic weapon is called a nuclear bomb, so the word describes such a device.

clue.text: Mineral bottle peripherally kept open for everybody in boiling taxi

indicators.note: kept means the bottle's edge letters hold everything else
peripherally takes the outer letters of the word bottle
in puts the rating letter inside the churned taxi letters
boiling suggests the letters of taxi are churned up

parts.note: U is the British film rating for universal, open to all

explanation.surface: A mineral bottle was kept unsealed for everyone in a hot taxi.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boiling' turns TAXI to AXIT, 'in' puts U inside it to give AUXIT, and 'kept' wraps B...E (the ends of 'bottle') round that.
explanation.definitionFit: Bauxite is the clay-like ore from which aluminium is extracted, a mineral.

clue.text: Agent of filmmaker who praises meals

parts.note: someone who praises with applause is a clapper
board means meals provided, as in bed and board

explanation.surface: A film director's representative applauds the catering.
explanation.definitionFit: A clapperboard is the hinged board snapped at the start of each take to sync film and sound.
